nodes.statement: Here, in the middle step we used~\eqref{cond-dec}, and in the last step we used the definitions of $\dist{-}{-}$ and $\I{-}$.
nodes.statement_short: Justify the steps

nodes.name: Distance to a sum or a fibre (Lemma 5.2)
nodes.statement: Let $X, Y, Z$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group, and with $Y, Z$ independent. Then we have\footnote{We thank Floris van Doorn for noting a sign discrepancy in a previous version of this statement, which was uncovered as part of the effort to formalize the results of this paper in {\tt Lean 4}.} \begin{align}\nonumber \dist{X}{Y - Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Y}) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y} \end{align} and \begin{align}\nonumber \dist{X}{Y|Y-Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Z}\bigr) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Replacing $Y$ by $Y-Z$, or by $(Y|Y-Z)$, raises the distance to $X$ by at most $\frac12 d[Y;Z]\pm\frac14(H[Z]-H[Y])$.
assumptions: $X, Y, Z$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group
with $Y, Z$ independent
conclusions: \begin{align}\nonumber \dist{X}{Y - Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Y}) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y} \end{align}
\begin{align}\nonumber \dist{X}{Y|Y-Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Z}\bigr) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z}.
nodes.label: first-useful

nodes.name: Distance to a sum (5.5)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \dist{X}{Y - Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Y}) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y}
nodes.label: lem51-a

nodes.name: Distance to a fibre (5.6)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \dist{X}{Y|Y-Z} - \dist{X}{Y} & \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \bigl(\ent{Y-Z} - \ent{Z}\bigr) \\ & = \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{Y}{Z} + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Y} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{Z}.
nodes.label: ruzsa-3

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.2
nodes.statement: We first prove~\eqref{lem51-a}. We may assume (taking an independent copy) that $X$ is independent of $Y, Z$. Then we have \begin{align*} \dist{X}{Y-Z} & - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & = \ent{X - Y + Z} - \ent{X-Y} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y - Z} + \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{Y}.\end{align*} Combining this with~\eqref{kv-2} (applied with $Y$ replaced by $-Y$) gives the required bound. The second form of the result is immediate from the definition of $\dist{Y}{Z}$, since $Y, Z$ are independent. Turning to~\eqref{ruzsa-3}, we have \begin{align*} \I{Y : Y-Z} & = \ent{Y} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y, Y - Z} \\ & = \ent{Y} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y, Z} = \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Z},\end{align*} and so~\eqref{ruzsa-3} is a consequence of~\Cref{cond-dist-fact}. Once again the second form of the result is immediate from the definition of $\dist{Y}{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: (5.5) from the Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman inequality; (5.6) from Lemma 5.1 with $I[Y:Y-Z]=H[Y-Z]-H[Z]$.

nodes.name: Make X independent of Y, Z
nodes.statement: We first prove~\eqref{lem51-a}. We may assume (taking an independent copy) that $X$ is independent of $Y, Z$.
nodes.statement_short: Make X independent of Y, Z

nodes.name: Write the difference in entropies
nodes.statement: Then we have \begin{align*} \dist{X}{Y-Z} & - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & = \ent{X - Y + Z} - \ent{X-Y} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y - Z} + \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{Y}.\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Write the difference in entropies

nodes.name: Apply the Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman inequality
nodes.statement: Combining this with~\eqref{kv-2} (applied with $Y$ replaced by $-Y$) gives the required bound. The second form of the result is immediate from the definition of $\dist{Y}{Z}$, since $Y, Z$ are independent.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman inequality

nodes.name: Compute I[Y:Y-Z] and apply Lemma 5.1
nodes.statement: Turning to~\eqref{ruzsa-3}, we have \begin{align*} \I{Y : Y-Z} & = \ent{Y} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y, Y - Z} \\ & = \ent{Y} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y, Z} = \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Z},\end{align*} and so~\eqref{ruzsa-3} is a consequence of~\Cref{cond-dist-fact}. Once again the second form of the result is immediate from the definition of $\dist{Y}{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute I[Y:Y-Z] and apply Lemma 5.1

nodes.name: Return to (5.3)
nodes.statement: We return to our main task of establishing~\eqref{suff-for-first-est}, and hence~\eqref{first-est}.
nodes.statement_short: Return to (5.3)

nodes.name: Lemma 5.2 bounds the four penalty terms
nodes.statement: As usual, in the main setting $G=\mathbf{F}_2^n$ we may replace all minus signs with plus signs in the statement of \Cref{first-useful}. Hence by \Cref{first-useful} (and recalling that $k$ is defined to be $\dist{X_1}{X_2}$) we have \[ \dist{X^0_1}{X_1+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1},\] \[ \dist{X^0_2}{X_2+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2},\] \begin{equation} \dist{X_1^0}{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \dist{X_2^0}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2}k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.2 bounds the four penalty terms

nodes.name: Penalty bound for the first fibre (5.7)
nodes.statement: \dist{X_1^0}{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2}
nodes.label: second-dist1

nodes.name: Penalty bound for the second fibre (5.8)
nodes.statement: \dist{X_2^0}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2}k + \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_2} - \tfrac{1}{4} \ent{X_1}.
nodes.label: second-dist2

nodes.name: Add the four bounds
nodes.statement: Adding all these inequalities, we obtain~\eqref{suff-for-first-est}.
nodes.statement_short: Add the four bounds

nodes.name: Entropy of the four-fold sum (HS bound)
nodes.statement: For use in the next two sections, we note that subtracting~\eqref{second-tc2} from~\eqref{second-main}, and combining the resulting inequality with~\eqref{second-dist1} and~\eqref{second-dist2} gives the bound \[ \dist{X_1+\tilde X_2}{X_2+\tilde X_1} \leqslant (1 + \eta) k - I_1, \] which is equivalent to \begin{equation} \bigH{X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1}+\tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2} + (2 + \eta) k - I_1. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $H[X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2]\le\frac12H[X_1]+\frac12H[X_2]+(2+\eta)k-I_1$.

nodes.name: Entropy of the four-fold sum (5.9)
nodes.statement: \bigH{X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1}+\tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2} + (2 + \eta) k - I_1.
nodes.label: HS-bound

nodes.name: Proof of the second estimate (Section 6)
nodes.statement: In this section we establish the upper bound~\eqref{second-est}, which was \[ I_2 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2 \eta (2 \eta k - I_1)}{1 - \eta}. \] We apply \Cref{cor-fibre} (and Remark \ref{rem:char2}), but now with the choice \[ (Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4) \coloneqq (X_2, X_1, \tilde X_2, \tilde X_1). \] Now \Cref{cor-fibre} can be rewritten as \begin{align*} &\dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} + \bigdist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &\quad + \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 \,|\, X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = 2k, \end{align*} recalling once again that $k \coloneqq \dist{X_1}{X_2}$. From~\eqref{to-contradict} and~\eqref{to-contradict-avg} as before, one has \begin{align} \nonumber \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X_1+\tilde X_1} \\ &- \costb{X_2+\tilde X_2} \end{align} and \begin{align*} \dist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1} \\& - \costb{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} . \end{align*} Now \Cref{first-useful} gives \begin{equation} \dist{X^0_1}{X_1+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_1}{X_1},\end{equation} \begin{equation} \dist{X^0_2}{X_2+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_2}{X_2}, \end{equation} \[ \dist{X^0_1}{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_1}{X_1}, \] and \[ \dist{X^0_2}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_2}{X_2}. \] Combining all these inequalities and cancelling terms, we obtain \begin{equation} \I{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant \eta ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ). \end{equation} One could bound the right-hand side by $4\eta k$ using the Ruzsa triangle inequality, but a more efficient approach is as follows. First, by combining~\eqref{1122},~\eqref{1122a} and~\eqref{1122b}, we obtain \begin{equation} \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k - \frac{\eta}{2} ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ). \end{equation} We may also expand \begin{align*} & \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &= \ent{ X_1+\tilde X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1+\tilde X_1} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &= \ent{ X_1+\tilde X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2} \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad - \tfrac{1}{2} \left( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \right), \end{align*} and hence by~\eqref{HS-bound} \[ \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \leqslant (2+\eta) k - \tfrac{1}{2} \left( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \right) - I_1. \] Combining this bound with~\eqref{d12} we obtain \begin{equation} \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \leqslant 2 k + \frac{2(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}. \end{equation} Therefore by~\eqref{combined} we have the desired bound \[ \I{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2\eta(2\eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Test the hypothesis on the pairs (3.2), (3.4) via the fibring identity with $(X_2,X_1,\tilde X_2,\tilde X_1)$. Bound $d[X_1;X_1]+d[X_2;X_2]$ through the four-fold sum bound (5.9) rather than the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: State the goal (3.14)
nodes.statement: In this section we establish the upper bound~\eqref{second-est}, which was \[ I_2 \coloneqq \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2 \eta (2 \eta k - I_1)}{1 - \eta}. \]
nodes.statement_short: State the goal (3.14)

nodes.name: Fibring identity with (X2, X1, tX2, tX1)
nodes.statement: We apply \Cref{cor-fibre} (and Remark \ref{rem:char2}), but now with the choice \[ (Y_1,Y_2,Y_3,Y_4) \coloneqq (X_2, X_1, \tilde X_2, \tilde X_1). \] Now \Cref{cor-fibre} can be rewritten as \begin{align*} &\dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} + \bigdist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &\quad + \bigI{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 \,|\, X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } = 2k, \end{align*} recalling once again that $k \coloneqq \dist{X_1}{X_2}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fibring identity with (X2, X1, tX2, tX1)

nodes.name: Apply the hypothesis to the sum and fibre pairs
nodes.statement: From~\eqref{to-contradict} and~\eqref{to-contradict-avg} as before, one has \begin{align} \nonumber \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X_1+\tilde X_1} \\ &- \costb{X_2+\tilde X_2} \end{align} and \begin{align*} \dist{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1} \\& - \costb{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the hypothesis to the sum and fibre pairs

nodes.name: Hypothesis on the sum pair (6.1)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k &- \costa{X_1+\tilde X_1} \\ &- \costb{X_2+\tilde X_2}

nodes.name: Lemma 5.2 bounds the penalties by d[Xi;Xi]/2
nodes.statement: Now \Cref{first-useful} gives \begin{equation} \dist{X^0_1}{X_1+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_1}{X_1},\end{equation} \begin{equation} \dist{X^0_2}{X_2+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_2}{X_2}, \end{equation} \[ \dist{X^0_1}{X_1|X_1+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_1}{X_1}, \] and \[ \dist{X^0_2}{X_2|X_2+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_2}{X_2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.2 bounds the penalties by d[Xi;Xi]/2

nodes.name: Penalty bound (6.2)
nodes.statement: \dist{X^0_1}{X_1+\tilde X_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_1}{X_1},
nodes.label: 1122a

nodes.name: Penalty bound (6.3)
nodes.statement: \dist{X^0_2}{X_2+\tilde X_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} \dist{X_2}{X_2},
nodes.label: 1122b

nodes.name: Combine to bound I_2 by eta(d[X1;X1]+d[X2;X2])
nodes.statement: Combining all these inequalities and cancelling terms, we obtain \begin{equation} \I{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant \eta ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Combine to bound I_2 by eta(d[X1;X1]+d[X2;X2])

nodes.name: I_2 bounded by self-distances (6.4)
nodes.statement: \I{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant \eta ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ).
nodes.label: combined

nodes.name: Lower bound (6.5) for the sum distance
nodes.statement: One could bound the right-hand side by $4\eta k$ using the Ruzsa triangle inequality, but a more efficient approach is as follows. First, by combining~\eqref{1122},~\eqref{1122a} and~\eqref{1122b}, we obtain \begin{equation} \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k - \frac{\eta}{2} ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound (6.5) for the sum distance

nodes.name: Lower bound on the sum distance (6.5)
nodes.statement: \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \geqslant k - \frac{\eta}{2} ( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} ).
nodes.label: d12

nodes.name: Upper bound via the four-fold sum bound (5.9)
nodes.statement: We may also expand \begin{align*} & \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &= \ent{ X_1+\tilde X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1+\tilde X_1} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2+\tilde X_2} \\ &= \ent{ X_1+\tilde X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_2} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X_2} \\ & \qquad\qquad\qquad - \tfrac{1}{2} \left( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \right), \end{align*} and hence by~\eqref{HS-bound} \[ \dist{X_1+\tilde X_1}{X_2+\tilde X_2} \leqslant (2+\eta) k - \tfrac{1}{2} \left( \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \right) - I_1. \]
nodes.statement_short: Upper bound via the four-fold sum bound (5.9)

nodes.name: Bound d[X1;X1]+d[X2;X2] (6.6)
nodes.statement: Combining this bound with~\eqref{d12} we obtain \begin{equation} \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \leqslant 2 k + \frac{2(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound d[X1;X1]+d[X2;X2] (6.6)

nodes.name: Bound on the self-distances (6.6)
nodes.statement: \dist{X_1}{X_1} + \dist{X_2}{X_2} \leqslant 2 k + \frac{2(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}.
nodes.label: x12

nodes.name: Conclude (3.14)
nodes.statement: Therefore by~\eqref{combined} we have the desired bound \[ \I{ X_1+X_2 : X_1 + \tilde X_1 | X_1+X_2+\tilde X_1+\tilde X_2 } \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2\eta(2\eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Conclude (3.14)

nodes.name: Endgame: proof of Proposition 2.1 (Section 7)
nodes.statement_short: Under the hypothesis, feed $T_i=(U|S=s),(V|S=s),(W|S=s)$ with $U+V+W=0$ (characteristic 2) into Lemma 7.2. With the first and second estimates this gives $k\le(8\eta+\eta^2)k$, so $k=0$.

nodes.name: Lemma 7.1
nodes.statement: In this section we conclude the proof of \Cref{de-prop}. Let us begin by recording an inequality which will be used several times in the calculations below. \begin{lemma} Let $X, Y, Z, Z'$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group, and with $Y, Z, Z'$ independent. Then we have \begin{align}\nonumber & \dist{X}{Y - Z | Y - Z - Z'} - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & \qquad \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} ( \ent{Y - Z - Z'} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y} - \ent{Z'}). \end{align} \end{lemma} \begin{proof} By~\eqref{ruzsa-3} (with a change of variables) we have \[ \dist{X}{Y - Z | Y - Z - Z'} - \dist{X}{Y - Z} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2}( \ent{Y - Z - Z'} - \ent{Z'}).\] Adding this to~\eqref{lem51-a} gives the result. \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7.1

nodes.name: Distance to a fibre of a double sum (Lemma 7.1)
nodes.statement: Let $X, Y, Z, Z'$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group, and with $Y, Z, Z'$ independent. Then we have \begin{align}\nonumber & \dist{X}{Y - Z | Y - Z - Z'} - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & \qquad \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} ( \ent{Y - Z - Z'} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y} - \ent{Z'}). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Bound on $d[X;Y-Z|Y-Z-Z']-d[X;Y]$ for independent $Y,Z,Z'$.
assumptions: $X, Y, Z, Z'$ be random variables taking values in some abelian group
with $Y, Z, Z'$ independent
conclusions: \begin{align}\nonumber & \dist{X}{Y - Z | Y - Z - Z'} - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & \qquad \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} ( \ent{Y - Z - Z'} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y} - \ent{Z'}). \end{align}
nodes.label: second-useful

nodes.name: Double-sum fibre bound (7.1)
nodes.statement: \nonumber & \dist{X}{Y - Z | Y - Z - Z'} - \dist{X}{Y} \\ & \qquad \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} ( \ent{Y - Z - Z'} + \ent{Y - Z} - \ent{Y} - \ent{Z'}).

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.1
nodes.statement: By~\eqref{ruzsa-3} (with a change of variables) we have \[ \dist{X}{Y - Z | Y - Z - Z'} - \dist{X}{Y - Z} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2}( \ent{Y - Z - Z'} - \ent{Z'}).\] Adding this to~\eqref{lem51-a} gives the result.
nodes.statement_short: Add the fibre bound (5.6), after a change of variables, to the sum bound (5.5).

nodes.name: Introduce U, V, W and S
nodes.statement: Turning now to the main argument, let $X_1,X_2,\tilde X_1,\tilde X_2$ be as before, and introduce the random variables \[ U \coloneqq X_1 + X_2, \qquad V \coloneqq \tilde X_1 + X_2, \qquad W \coloneqq X_1 + \tilde X_1\] and \[ S \coloneqq X_1 + X_2 + \tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2.\]
nodes.statement_short: Introduce U, V, W and S

nodes.name: Express I_1, I_2, I_3 through U, V, W, S
nodes.statement: From the definitions~\eqref{first-est-a},~\eqref{second-est-a},~\eqref{third-est-a} of $I_1, I_2, I_3$ and the above notation, we see that \[ I_1 = \I{U : V \, | \, S}, \qquad I_2 = \I{W : U \, | \, S}, \qquad I_3 = \I{V : W \, | \,S}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Express I_1, I_2, I_3 through U, V, W, S

nodes.name: Recall the first estimate
nodes.statement: Recall from~\eqref{first-est} that $I_1 \leqslant 2 \eta k$.
nodes.statement_short: Recall the first estimate

nodes.name: Sum of the three conditional mutual informations (7.2)
nodes.statement: From~\eqref{second-est} (and since $I_2 = I_3$) we have the inequalities \[ \I{V : W \, | \,S} , \; \I{W : U \, | \, S} \leqslant 2 \eta k + \frac{2\eta(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta} . \] Summing these two inequalities and the equality $\I{U : V \, | \, S} = I_1$ gives \begin{align} \nonumber \I{U : V \, | \, S} + \I{V : W \, | \,S} &+ \I{W : U \, | \, S}\\ \nonumber &\leqslant I_1+4\eta k+ \frac{4\eta(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}\\ &= 6 \eta k - \frac{1 - 5 \eta}{1-\eta} (2 \eta k - I_1). \end{align} We encourage the reader to read the argument assuming first that $I_1 = 2 \eta k$, in which case the calculations are cleaner.
nodes.statement_short: Sum of the three conditional mutual informations (7.2)

nodes.name: Sum of conditional mutual informations of U, V, W (7.2)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \I{U : V \, | \, S} + \I{V : W \, | \,S} &+ \I{W : U \, | \, S}\\ \nonumber &\leqslant I_1+4\eta k+ \frac{4\eta(2 \eta k - I_1)}{1-\eta}\\ &= 6 \eta k - \frac{1 - 5 \eta}{1-\eta} (2 \eta k - I_1).
nodes.label: uvw-s

nodes.name: Lemma 7.1 bounds the penalties of U|S, V|S, W|S
nodes.statement: We assemble some preliminary estimates on distances. By \Cref{second-useful} (again replacing all minus signs with plus signs, and taking $X = X_1^0$, $Y = X_1$, $Z = X_2$ and $Z' = \tilde X_1 + \tilde X_2$, so that $Y + Z = U$ and $Y + Z + Z' = S$) we have, noting that $\ent{Y+Z} = \ent{Z'}$, \[ \dist{X^0_1}{U|S} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{S} - \ent{X_1}). \] Further applications of \Cref{second-useful} give \begin{align*} \dist{X^0_2}{U|S} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} &\leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{S} - \ent{X_2}) \\ \dist{X^0_1}{V|S} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} &\leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{S} - \ent{X_1})\\ \dist{X^0_2}{V|S} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} &\leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{S} - \ent{X_2}) \end{align*} and \[ \dist{X^0_1}{W|S} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{S} + \ent{W} - \ent{X_1} - \ent{W'}),\] where $W' := X_2 + \tilde X_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7.1 bounds the penalties of U|S, V|S, W|S

nodes.name: Penalty of W|S via W'
nodes.statement: To treat $\dist{X^0_2}{W|S}$, first note that this equals $\dist{X^0_2}{W'|S}$, since for a fixed choice $s$ of $S$ we have $W' = W + s$. Now we may apply \Cref{second-useful} to obtain \[ \dist{X^0_2}{W'|S} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} (\ent{S} + \ent{W'} - \ent{X_2} - \ent{W}).\]
nodes.statement_short: Penalty of W|S via W'

nodes.name: Total penalty bound (7.3)
nodes.statement: Summing these six estimates and using~\eqref{HS-bound}, we conclude that \begin{align} \nonumber \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A\in\{U,V,W\}} \big(\dist{X^0_i}{A|S} & - \dist{X^0_i}{X_i}\big) \\ &\leqslant 3\ent{S} - \tfrac{3}{2} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{3}{2}\ent{X_2} \nonumber \\ &\leqslant (6 - 3\eta) k + 3(2 \eta k - I_1). \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Total penalty bound (7.3)

nodes.name: Total penalty bound (7.3)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A\in\{U,V,W\}} \big(\dist{X^0_i}{A|S} & - \dist{X^0_i}{X_i}\big) \\ &\leqslant 3\ent{S} - \tfrac{3}{2} \ent{X_1} - \tfrac{3}{2}\ent{X_2} \nonumber \\ &\leqslant (6 - 3\eta) k + 3(2 \eta k - I_1).
nodes.label: total-dist

nodes.name: Key observation U + V + W = 0 (characteristic 2)
nodes.statement: Now we come to the key observation we will exploit, which is that \begin{equation} U + V + W = 0. \end{equation} Here, of course, we are using the fact that we are in characteristic $2$. This is the only critical use of this fact in the argument, in the sense that it cannot be avoided by judicious insertion of negative signs or by accepting slightly worse constants by invoking the inequality $\dist{X}{-Y} \leqslant 3 \dist{X}{Y}$ (see~\cite[Equation 17]{tao-entropy}) and related estimates.
nodes.statement_short: Key observation U + V + W = 0 (characteristic 2)

nodes.name: Lemma 7.2
nodes.statement: To see the force of~\eqref{uvw-s} and~\eqref{uvw-sum}, we state the following general claim. \begin{lemma} Let $G=\mathbf{F}_2^n$ and let $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ be a $G^3$-valued random variable such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically. Set \begin{equation} \delta \coloneqq \sum_{1 \leqslant i < j \leqslant 3} \I{T_i;T_j}. \end{equation} Then there exist random variables $T'_1, T'_2$ such that \begin{align*} \dist{T'_1}{T'_2} + & \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{T'_1} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1}) + \eta(\dist{X_2^0}{T'_2} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2}) \\ & \leqslant \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (\dist{X^0_i}{T_j} - \dist{X^0_i}{X_i}) \biggr). \end{align*} \end{lemma} We recommend that the reader first work through this proof in the case $\delta = 0$, when the variables $T_1, T_2, T_3$ are independent. Recalling~\eqref{eq:i-eq-0}, the proof below collapses to taking $T'_1,T'_2$ to be some two of $\{T_1,T_2,T_3\}$, without the need to apply \Cref{lem-bsg}. \begin{proof} We apply the variant of the entropic Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers theorem stated in \Cref{lem-bsg}, taking $(A,B) = (T_1, T_2)$ there. Since $T_1 + T_2 = T_3$, the conclusion is that \begin{align} \nonumber \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) & \dist{(T_1 | T_3 = t_3)}{(T_2 | T_3 = t_3)} \\ & \leqslant 3 \I{T_1 : T_2} + 2 \ent{T_3} - \ent{T_1} - \ent{T_2}. \end{align} The right-hand side in~\eqref{bsg-t1t2} can be rearranged as \begin{align*} & 2( \ent{T_1} + \ent{T_2} + \ent{T_3}) - 3 \ent{T_1,T_2} \\ & = 2(\ent{T_1} + \ent{T_2} + \ent{T_3}) - \ent{T_1,T_2} - \ent{T_2,T_3} - \ent{T_1, T_3} = \delta,\end{align*} using the fact that all three terms $\ent{T_i,T_j}$ are equal to $\ent{T_1,T_2,T_3}$ and hence to each other. We also have \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) \bigl(\dist{X^0_1}{(T_1 | T_3=t_3)} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1}\bigr) \\ &\quad = \dist{X^0_1}{T_1 | T_3} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \dist{X^0_1}{T_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{T_1 : T_3} \end{align*} by \Cref{cond-dist-fact}, and similarly \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) (\dist{X^0_2}{(T_2 | T_3=t_3)} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2}) \\ &\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad \leqslant \dist{X^0_2}{T_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{T_2 : T_3}. \end{align*} Temporarily define \[ \psi[Y_1; Y_2] \coloneqq \dist{Y_1}{Y_2} + \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{Y_1} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1}) + \eta(\dist{X_2^0}{Y_2} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2}).\] Putting the above observations together, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) \psi[(T_1 | T_3=t_3); (T_2 | T_3=t_3)] \leqslant \delta + \eta (\dist{X^0_1}{T_1}-\dist{X^0_1}{X_1}) \\ + \eta (\dist{X^0_2}{T_2}-\dist{X^0_2}{X_2}) + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_1:T_3} + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_2:T_3}. \end{align*} Choosing some $t_3$ in the support of $T_3$ that minimizes the $\psi[-;-]$ value, and setting $T'_{1,3} \coloneqq (T_1 | T_3 = t_3)$, $T'_{2,3} \coloneqq (T_2 | T_3 = t_3)$, we have \begin{align}\nonumber \psi[T_{1,3}';T_{2,3}'] \leqslant \delta + \eta (& \dist{X^0_1}{T_1}-\dist{X^0_1}{X_1}) + \eta (\dist{X^0_2}{T_2}-\dist{X^0_2}{X_2}) \\ & + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_1:T_3} + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_2:T_3}. \end{align} We now repeat this analysis for all permutations of $\{T_1,T_2,T_3\}$ to get variables $T'_{\alpha,\gamma}, T'_{\beta,\gamma}$ for $\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\}$ ranging over all six permutations of $\{1,2,3\}$. Averaging the resulting inequalities~\eqref{eq:t1323}, and recalling the definition~\eqref{delta-t1t2t3-def} of $\delta$, we get \[ \tfrac16 \sum_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma} \psi[T_{\alpha,\gamma}';T_{\beta,\gamma}'] \leqslant \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (\dist{X^0_i}{T_j}-\dist{X^0_i}{X_i}) \biggr), \] from which the result follows (taking $T'_1,T'_2$ to be $T'_{\alpha,\gamma},T'_{\beta,\gamma}$ for some $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ that gives at most the average value). \end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7.2

nodes.name: Endgame lemma for a trio summing to zero (Lemma 7.2)
nodes.statement: Let $G=\mathbf{F}_2^n$ and let $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ be a $G^3$-valued random variable such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically. Set \begin{equation} \delta \coloneqq \sum_{1 \leqslant i < j \leqslant 3} \I{T_i;T_j}. \end{equation} Then there exist random variables $T'_1, T'_2$ such that \begin{align*} \dist{T'_1}{T'_2} + & \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{T'_1} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1}) + \eta(\dist{X_2^0}{T'_2} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2}) \\ & \leqslant \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (\dist{X^0_i}{T_j} - \dist{X^0_i}{X_i}) \biggr). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: If $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$, some pair $T'_1,T'_2$ has $\tau$-type cost at most $\delta$ plus $\eta/3$ times penalties, $\delta$ the pairwise mutual informations.
assumptions: $G=\mathbf{F}_2^n$
$(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ be a $G^3$-valued random variable such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically
conclusions: there exist random variables $T'_1, T'_2$ such that \begin{align*} \dist{T'_1}{T'_2} + & \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{T'_1} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1}) + \eta(\dist{X_2^0}{T'_2} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2}) \\ & \leqslant \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (\dist{X^0_i}{T_j} - \dist{X^0_i}{X_i}) \biggr). \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:abstract

nodes.name: Definition of delta (7.5)
nodes.statement: \delta \coloneqq \sum_{1 \leqslant i < j \leqslant 3} \I{T_i;T_j}.
nodes.label: delta-t1t2t3-def

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7.2
nodes.statement: We apply the variant of the entropic Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers theorem stated in \Cref{lem-bsg}, taking $(A,B) = (T_1, T_2)$ there. Since $T_1 + T_2 = T_3$, the conclusion is that \begin{align} \nonumber \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) & \dist{(T_1 | T_3 = t_3)}{(T_2 | T_3 = t_3)} \\ & \leqslant 3 \I{T_1 : T_2} + 2 \ent{T_3} - \ent{T_1} - \ent{T_2}.\end{align} The right-hand side in~\eqref{bsg-t1t2} can be rearranged as \begin{align*} & 2( \ent{T_1} + \ent{T_2} + \ent{T_3}) - 3 \ent{T_1,T_2} \\ & = 2(\ent{T_1} + \ent{T_2} + \ent{T_3}) - \ent{T_1,T_2} - \ent{T_2,T_3} - \ent{T_1, T_3} = \delta,\end{align*} using the fact that all three terms $\ent{T_i,T_j}$ are equal to $\ent{T_1,T_2,T_3}$ and hence to each other. We also have \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) \bigl(\dist{X^0_1}{(T_1 | T_3=t_3)} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1}\bigr) \\ &\quad = \dist{X^0_1}{T_1 | T_3} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \dist{X^0_1}{T_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{T_1 : T_3} \end{align*} by \Cref{cond-dist-fact}, and similarly \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) (\dist{X^0_2}{(T_2 | T_3=t_3)} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2}) \\ &\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad \leqslant \dist{X^0_2}{T_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{T_2 : T_3}. \end{align*} Temporarily define \[ \psi[Y_1; Y_2] \coloneqq \dist{Y_1}{Y_2} + \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{Y_1} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1}) + \eta(\dist{X_2^0}{Y_2} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2}).\] Putting the above observations together, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) \psi[(T_1 | T_3=t_3); (T_2 | T_3=t_3)] \leqslant \delta + \eta (\dist{X^0_1}{T_1}-\dist{X^0_1}{X_1}) \\ + \eta (\dist{X^0_2}{T_2}-\dist{X^0_2}{X_2}) + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_1:T_3} + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_2:T_3}. \end{align*} Choosing some $t_3$ in the support of $T_3$ that minimizes the $\psi[-;-]$ value, and setting $T'_{1,3} \coloneqq (T_1 | T_3 = t_3)$, $T'_{2,3} \coloneqq (T_2 | T_3 = t_3)$, we have \begin{align}\nonumber \psi[T_{1,3}';T_{2,3}'] \leqslant \delta + \eta (& \dist{X^0_1}{T_1}-\dist{X^0_1}{X_1}) + \eta (\dist{X^0_2}{T_2}-\dist{X^0_2}{X_2}) \\ & + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_1:T_3} + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_2:T_3}. \end{align} We now repeat this analysis for all permutations of $\{T_1,T_2,T_3\}$ to get variables $T'_{\alpha,\gamma}, T'_{\beta,\gamma}$ for $\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\}$ ranging over all six permutations of $\{1,2,3\}$. Averaging the resulting inequalities~\eqref{eq:t1323}, and recalling the definition~\eqref{delta-t1t2t3-def} of $\delta$, we get \[ \tfrac16 \sum_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma} \psi[T_{\alpha,\gamma}';T_{\beta,\gamma}'] \leqslant \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (\dist{X^0_i}{T_j}-\dist{X^0_i}{X_i}) \biggr), \] from which the result follows (taking $T'_1,T'_2$ to be $T'_{\alpha,\gamma},T'_{\beta,\gamma}$ for some $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ that gives at most the average value).
nodes.statement_short: Apply entropic BSG to $(T_1,T_2)$ with $T_1+T_2=T_3$, pick a good fibre $t_3$, and average over the six permutations.

nodes.name: Entropic BSG applied to (T1, T2)
nodes.statement: We apply the variant of the entropic Balog--Szemer\'edi--Gowers theorem stated in \Cref{lem-bsg}, taking $(A,B) = (T_1, T_2)$ there. Since $T_1 + T_2 = T_3$, the conclusion is that \begin{align} \nonumber \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) & \dist{(T_1 | T_3 = t_3)}{(T_2 | T_3 = t_3)} \\ & \leqslant 3 \I{T_1 : T_2} + 2 \ent{T_3} - \ent{T_1} - \ent{T_2}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Entropic BSG applied to (T1, T2)

nodes.name: The right-hand side equals delta
nodes.statement: The right-hand side in~\eqref{bsg-t1t2} can be rearranged as \begin{align*} & 2( \ent{T_1} + \ent{T_2} + \ent{T_3}) - 3 \ent{T_1,T_2} \\ & = 2(\ent{T_1} + \ent{T_2} + \ent{T_3}) - \ent{T_1,T_2} - \ent{T_2,T_3} - \ent{T_1, T_3} = \delta,\end{align*} using the fact that all three terms $\ent{T_i,T_j}$ are equal to $\ent{T_1,T_2,T_3}$ and hence to each other.
nodes.statement_short: The right-hand side equals delta

nodes.name: Lemma 5.1 bounds the penalties of the fibres
nodes.statement: We also have \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) \bigl(\dist{X^0_1}{(T_1 | T_3=t_3)} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1}\bigr) \\ &\quad = \dist{X^0_1}{T_1 | T_3} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} \leqslant \dist{X^0_1}{T_1} - \dist{X^0_1}{X_1} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{T_1 : T_3} \end{align*} by \Cref{cond-dist-fact}, and similarly \begin{align*} & \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) (\dist{X^0_2}{(T_2 | T_3=t_3)} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2}) \\ &\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad\quad \leqslant \dist{X^0_2}{T_2} - \dist{X^0_2}{X_2} + \tfrac{1}{2} \I{T_2 : T_3}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 5.1 bounds the penalties of the fibres

nodes.name: Define psi
nodes.statement: Temporarily define \[ \psi[Y_1; Y_2] \coloneqq \dist{Y_1}{Y_2} + \eta (\dist{X_1^0}{Y_1} - \dist{X_1^0}{X_1}) + \eta(\dist{X_2^0}{Y_2} - \dist{X_2^0}{X_2}).\]
nodes.statement_short: Define psi

nodes.name: Average psi over t3
nodes.statement: Putting the above observations together, we have \begin{align*} \sum_{t_3}p_{T_3}(t_3) \psi[(T_1 | T_3=t_3); (T_2 | T_3=t_3)] \leqslant \delta + \eta (\dist{X^0_1}{T_1}-\dist{X^0_1}{X_1}) \\ + \eta (\dist{X^0_2}{T_2}-\dist{X^0_2}{X_2}) + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_1:T_3} + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_2:T_3}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Average psi over t3

nodes.name: Choose a fibre t3 minimising psi (7.7)
nodes.statement: Choosing some $t_3$ in the support of $T_3$ that minimizes the $\psi[-;-]$ value, and setting $T'_{1,3} \coloneqq (T_1 | T_3 = t_3)$, $T'_{2,3} \coloneqq (T_2 | T_3 = t_3)$, we have \begin{align}\nonumber \psi[T_{1,3}';T_{2,3}'] \leqslant \delta + \eta (& \dist{X^0_1}{T_1}-\dist{X^0_1}{X_1}) + \eta (\dist{X^0_2}{T_2}-\dist{X^0_2}{X_2}) \\ & + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_1:T_3} + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_2:T_3}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Choose a fibre t3 minimising psi (7.7)

nodes.name: Bound for the chosen fibre (7.7)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \psi[T_{1,3}';T_{2,3}'] \leqslant \delta + \eta (& \dist{X^0_1}{T_1}-\dist{X^0_1}{X_1}) + \eta (\dist{X^0_2}{T_2}-\dist{X^0_2}{X_2}) \\ & + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_1:T_3} + \tfrac12 \eta \I{T_2:T_3}.
nodes.label: eq:t1323

nodes.name: Average over the six permutations
nodes.statement: We now repeat this analysis for all permutations of $\{T_1,T_2,T_3\}$ to get variables $T'_{\alpha,\gamma}, T'_{\beta,\gamma}$ for $\{\alpha,\beta,\gamma\}$ ranging over all six permutations of $\{1,2,3\}$. Averaging the resulting inequalities~\eqref{eq:t1323}, and recalling the definition~\eqref{delta-t1t2t3-def} of $\delta$, we get \[ \tfrac16 \sum_{\alpha,\beta,\gamma} \psi[T_{\alpha,\gamma}';T_{\beta,\gamma}'] \leqslant \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (\dist{X^0_i}{T_j}-\dist{X^0_i}{X_i}) \biggr), \] from which the result follows (taking $T'_1,T'_2$ to be $T'_{\alpha,\gamma},T'_{\beta,\gamma}$ for some $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ that gives at most the average value).
nodes.statement_short: Average over the six permutations

nodes.name: Lemma 7.2 and the hypothesis give k <= delta + ...
nodes.statement: Applying \Cref{lem:abstract} with any random variables $(T_1,T_2,T_3)$ such that $T_1+T_2+T_3=0$ holds identically, and applying~\eqref{to-contradict} with $X'_1 = T'_1$, $X'_2 = T'_2$, we deduce that \[ k \leqslant \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{j = 1}^3 (\dist{X^0_i}{T_j} -\dist{X^0_i}{X_i}) \biggr). \] Note that $\delta$ is still defined by~\eqref{delta-t1t2t3-def} and thus depends on $T_1,T_2,T_3$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 7.2 and the hypothesis give k <= delta + ...

nodes.name: Apply to the fibres of U, V, W over S and average (7.8)
nodes.statement: In particular we may apply this for \[ T_1 = (U | S = s),\qquad T_2 = (V | S = s), \qquad T_3 = (W | S = s) \] for $s$ in the range of $S$ (which is a valid choice by~\eqref{uvw-sum}) and then average over $s$ with weights $p_S(s)$, to obtain \begin{equation} k \leqslant \tilde \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \tilde \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A\in\{U,V,W\}} \bigl( \dist{X^0_i}{A|S} - \dist{X^0_i}{X_i}\bigr) \biggr), \end{equation} where \[ \tilde \delta \coloneqq \I{U : V | S} + \I{V : W | S} + \I{W : U | S}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Apply to the fibres of U, V, W over S and average (7.8)

nodes.name: Averaged endgame bound (7.8)
nodes.statement: k \leqslant \tilde \delta + \frac{\eta}{3} \biggl( \tilde \delta + \sum_{i=1}^2 \sum_{A\in\{U,V,W\}} \bigl( \dist{X^0_i}{A|S} - \dist{X^0_i}{X_i}\bigr) \biggr),
nodes.label: almost-done

nodes.name: k <= (8 eta + eta^2) k
nodes.statement: Putting this together with~\eqref{uvw-s} and~\eqref{total-dist}, we conclude that \begin{align*} k &\leqslant \Bigl(1+\frac{\eta}{3}\Bigr)\Bigl(6\eta k-\frac{1-5\eta}{1-\eta}(2\eta k-I_1)\Bigr)+\frac{\eta}{3}\Bigl((6-3\eta)k+3(2\eta k-I_1)\Bigr)\\ &= (8\eta + \eta^2) k - \biggl( \frac{1 - 5 \eta}{1-\eta}\Bigl(1 + \frac{\eta}{3}\Bigr) - \eta \biggr)(2 \eta k - I_1)\\ &\leqslant (8 \eta + \eta^2) k \end{align*} since the quantity $2 \eta k - I_1$ is non-negative (by~\eqref{first-est}), and its coefficient in the above expression is non-positive provided that $\eta(2\eta + 17) \leqslant 3$, which is certainly the case for our choice $\eta = \frac{1}{9}$ (and in fact for any $\eta \leqslant \frac{1}{6}$).
nodes.statement_short: k <= (8 eta + eta^2) k

nodes.name: 8 eta + eta^2 < 1, so k = 0
nodes.statement: Moreover, for\footnote{In fact we can take any $\eta<\frac{1}{4 + \sqrt{17}} = \frac{1}{8.1231\dots}$, and the other constants in the paper can be improved accordingly. In \cite{liao1,liao2} the arguments were modified to also apply in the regime $\eta < \frac{1}{8}$.} $\eta=\tfrac{1}{9}$ we have $8 \eta + \eta^2 < 1$. It follows that $k=0$, as desired. The proof of \Cref{de-prop} (and hence of all our results) is complete.
nodes.statement_short: 8 eta + eta^2 < 1, so k = 0

nodes.name: Entropy at most log of support size
nodes.statement: First we remark that if $X$ takes values in a set $S$ then, by Jensen's inequality, \begin{equation} \ent{X} \leqslant \log |S|.\end{equation}

nodes.name: Jensen bound (A.1)
nodes.statement: \ent{X} \leqslant \log |S|.
nodes.label: convexity-bound

nodes.name: Largest atom at least exp(-H)
nodes.statement: Also, denoting by $p_X$ the density function of $X$, \[ \ent{X} = \sum_x p_X(x) \log \frac{1}{p_X(x)} \geqslant \min_{x : p_X(x)>0} \log \frac{1}{p_X(x)},\] and therefore \begin{equation} \max_x p_X(x) \geqslant e^{-\ent{X}}.\end{equation}

nodes.name: Largest atom bound (A.2)
nodes.statement: \max_x p_X(x) \geqslant e^{-\ent{X}}.
nodes.label: px-lower

nodes.name: Conditional entropy
nodes.statement: Given a pair $(X,Y)$ of random variables, the \emph{conditional entropy} $\ent{X|Y}$ is defined by the formula \[ \ent{X|Y} \coloneqq \sum_y p_Y(y) \ent{X|Y=y} \] where $y$ ranges over the support of $p_Y$, and $X|Y=y$ denotes the random variable $X$ conditioned on the event $Y=y$.

nodes.name: Chain rule for entropy
nodes.statement: \ent{X,Y} = \ent{X|Y} + \ent{Y}.
conclusions: \ent{X,Y} = \ent{X|Y} + \ent{Y}.
nodes.label: chain-rule

nodes.name: Abbreviation H[X,Y]
nodes.statement: Here we abbreviate $\ent{(X,Y)}$ as $\ent{X,Y}$, and will make similar abbreviations regarding other information-theoretic quantities in this paper without further comment; for instance, $\ent{(X,Y)|(Z,W)}$ becomes $\ent{X,Y|Z,W}$.

nodes.name: Conditional chain rule
nodes.statement: Note that~\eqref{chain-rule} implies a conditional generalization \[ \ent{X,Y|Z} = \ent{X|Y,Z} + \ent{Y|Z}. \] for all random variables $X,Y,Z$.

nodes.name: Mutual information
nodes.statement: The \emph{mutual information} $\I{X:Y}$ is defined by the formula \[ \begin{split} \I{X:Y} &= \ent{X} + \ent{Y} - \ent{X,Y} \\ &= \ent{X} - \ent{X|Y} \\ &= \ent{Y} - \ent{Y|X}, \end{split} \] and is non-negative by a standard application of Jensen's inequality, vanishing precisely when $X,Y$ are independent; in particular \begin{equation} \ent{X,Y} = \ent{X} + \ent{Y} \end{equation} if and only if $X,Y$ are independent, and \begin{equation} \ent{X | Y} \leqslant \ent{X}\end{equation} always.
nodes.statement_short: $I[X:Y]=H[X]+H[Y]-H[X,Y]\ge 0$, zero iff independent; hence (A.4) and $H[X|Y]\le H[X]$.

nodes.name: Entropy of independent pair (A.4)
nodes.statement: \ent{X,Y} = \ent{X} + \ent{Y}
nodes.label: indep

nodes.name: Conditioning reduces entropy (A.5)
nodes.statement: \ent{X | Y} \leqslant \ent{X}
nodes.label: cond-dec

nodes.name: Submodularity of entropy
nodes.statement: Suppose now that $(X,Y,Z)$ is a triple of random variables. Applying~\eqref{cond-dec} to $(X | Z = z)$ and summing over $z$ (weighted by $p_Z(z)$) gives \begin{equation} \ent{X | Y, Z} \leqslant \ent{X | Z},\end{equation} which is known as \emph{submodularity}. It may equivalently be written as \begin{equation} \ent{X,Y,Z} + \ent{Z} \leqslant \ent{X,Z} + \ent{Y,Z}.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $H[X|Y,Z]\le H[X|Z]$, equivalently $H[X,Y,Z]+H[Z]\le H[X,Z]+H[Y,Z]$.

nodes.name: Submodularity (A.6)
nodes.statement: \ent{X | Y, Z} \leqslant \ent{X | Z},
nodes.label: submodularity-first

nodes.name: Submodularity, joint form (A.7)
nodes.statement: \ent{X,Y,Z} + \ent{Z} \leqslant \ent{X,Z} + \ent{Y,Z}.
nodes.label: submod-basic

nodes.name: Conditional mutual information
nodes.statement: The \emph{conditional mutual information} $\I{X:Y|Z}$ is defined by \[ \I{X:Y|Z} \coloneqq \sum_z p_Z(z) \I{ (X|Z=z) : (Y|Z=z)}. \]

nodes.name: Non-negativity of conditional mutual information
nodes.statement: Submodularity is equivalent to the statement that \begin{equation} \I{X:Y|Z} \geqslant 0, \end{equation} since \begin{equation} \I{X:Y|Z} = \ent{X,Z} + \ent{Y,Z} - \ent{X,Y,Z} - \ent{Z}.\end{equation}

nodes.name: I[X:Y|Z] >= 0 (A.8)
nodes.statement: \I{X:Y|Z} \geqslant 0,
nodes.label: nonneg-cond

nodes.name: Conditional mutual information formula (A.9)
nodes.statement: \I{X:Y|Z} = \ent{X,Z} + \ent{Y,Z} - \ent{X,Y,Z} - \ent{Z}.
nodes.label: cond-form-mutual-2

nodes.name: Equality case: conditional independence
nodes.statement: Equality occurs in~\eqref{nonneg-cond} (and hence in~\eqref{submod-basic}) if and only if $X,Y$ are conditionally independent relative to $Z$.

nodes.name: Sumset lower bound
nodes.statement: Whenever $X,Y$ are $G$-valued random variables, we have that \[ \ent{X\pm Y} \geqslant \ent{X\pm Y|Y} = \ent{X|Y} = \ent{X} - \I{X:Y} \] and similarly with the roles of $X,Y$ reversed, thus \begin{equation} \max(\ent{X}, \ent{Y}) - \I{X:Y} \leqslant \ent{X\pm Y}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Sumset lower bound (A.10)
nodes.statement: \max(\ent{X}, \ent{Y}) - \I{X:Y} \leqslant \ent{X\pm Y}.
nodes.label: sumset-lower-gen

nodes.name: Conditional sumset lower bound
nodes.statement: We note also the conditional variant of~\eqref{sumset-lower-gen}, namely \[ \max(\ent{X|Z}, \ent{Y|Z}) - \I{X:Y|Z} \leqslant \ent{X\pm Y|Z}, \] which follows from~\eqref{sumset-lower-gen} by conditioning on $Z = z$ and summing over $z$ (weighted by $p_Z(z)$).

nodes.name: Sumset lower bound for independent variables
nodes.statement: A particular consequence of~\eqref{sumset-lower-gen} is that \begin{equation} \max(\ent{X}, \ent{Y}) \leqslant \ent{X\pm Y} \end{equation} when $X,Y$ are independent.

nodes.name: max(H[X],H[Y]) <= H[X +- Y] (A.11)
nodes.statement: \max(\ent{X}, \ent{Y}) \leqslant \ent{X\pm Y}
nodes.label: sumset-lower

nodes.name: Entropy difference bounded by twice the distance
nodes.statement: Comparing this with~\eqref{sumset-lower} we see that \begin{equation} |\ent{X}-\ent{Y}| \leqslant 2\dist{X}{Y}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: |H[X]-H[Y]| <= 2 d[X;Y] (A.12)
nodes.statement: |\ent{X}-\ent{Y}| \leqslant 2\dist{X}{Y}.
nodes.label: ruzsa-diff

nodes.name: Sum entropy minus entropy bounded by twice the distance
nodes.statement: We may also deduce that \[ \ent{X-Y} - \ent{X}, \ent{X-Y} - \ent{Y} \leqslant 2\dist{X}{Y}. \]

nodes.name: Ruzsa triangle inequality
nodes.statement: The most important property of the Ruzsa distance is the (Ruzsa) triangle inequality \[ \dist{X}{Y} \leqslant \dist{X}{Z} + \dist{Z}{Y}.\]
nodes.origin_citation: Ruzsa 2009; Tao 2010 (Sumset and inverse sumset theory for Shannon entropy) (16)
conclusions: \[ \dist{X}{Y} \leqslant \dist{X}{Z} + \dist{Z}{Y}.\]

nodes.name: Proof of the Ruzsa triangle inequality
nodes.statement: This is equivalent to establishing \begin{equation} \ent{X - Y} \leqslant \ent{X-Z} + \ent{Z-Y} - \ent{Z}\end{equation} whenever $X, Y, Z$ are independent. To prove this, apply~\eqref{nonneg-cond} with a change of variables to get $\I{X-Z : Y | X - Y} \geqslant 0$ which, when written out in full, gives \[ \ent{X - Z, X - Y} + \ent{Y, X - Y} \geqslant \ent{X - Z, Y, X - Y} + \ent{X - Y}.\] Using \[ \ent{X - Z, X - Y} = \ent{X-Z, Y-Z} \leqslant \ent{X - Z} + \ent{Y - Z},\] \[ \ent{Y, X - Y} = \ent{X, Y}, \] and \[ \ent{X - Z, Y, X - Y} = \ent{X, Y, Z} = \ent{X, Y} + \ent{Z},\] and rearranging, we indeed obtain~\eqref{submod-explicit}. (As observed in~\cite{gmt}, we do not in fact use the independence of $X$ and $Y$ here.)
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to $H[X-Y]\le H[X-Z]+H[Z-Y]-H[Z]$ and get it from $I[X-Z:Y|X-Y]\ge 0$.

nodes.name: Reduce to the entropy inequality (A.13)
nodes.statement: This is equivalent to establishing \begin{equation} \ent{X - Y} \leqslant \ent{X-Z} + \ent{Z-Y} - \ent{Z}\end{equation} whenever $X, Y, Z$ are independent.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to the entropy inequality (A.13)

nodes.name: Entropy form of the triangle inequality (A.13)
nodes.statement: \ent{X - Y} \leqslant \ent{X-Z} + \ent{Z-Y} - \ent{Z}
nodes.label: submod-explicit

nodes.name: Non-negativity of I[X-Z:Y|X-Y]
nodes.statement: To prove this, apply~\eqref{nonneg-cond} with a change of variables to get $\I{X-Z : Y | X - Y} \geqslant 0$ which, when written out in full, gives \[ \ent{X - Z, X - Y} + \ent{Y, X - Y} \geqslant \ent{X - Z, Y, X - Y} + \ent{X - Y}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Non-negativity of I[X-Z:Y|X-Y]

nodes.name: Rewrite the entropies and rearrange
nodes.statement: Using \[ \ent{X - Z, X - Y} = \ent{X-Z, Y-Z} \leqslant \ent{X - Z} + \ent{Y - Z},\] \[ \ent{Y, X - Y} = \ent{X, Y}, \] and \[ \ent{X - Z, Y, X - Y} = \ent{X, Y, Z} = \ent{X, Y} + \ent{Z},\] and rearranging, we indeed obtain~\eqref{submod-explicit}. (As observed in~\cite{gmt}, we do not in fact use the independence of $X$ and $Y$ here.)
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the entropies and rearrange

nodes.name: Conditional Ruzsa distance
nodes.statement: If $(X, Z)$ and $(Y, W)$ are random variables (where $X$ and $Y$ are $G$-valued) we define \begin{equation} \dist{X | Z}{Y | W} \coloneqq \sum_{z,w} p_{Z}(z) p_{W}(w) \dist{(X| Z=z)}{(Y| W = w )}. \end{equation}
nodes.origin_citation: Tao 2010 (Sumset and inverse sumset theory for Shannon entropy); Green, Manners & Tao 2023 (Sumsets and entropy revisited)

nodes.name: Conditional distance (A.14)
nodes.statement: \dist{X | Z}{Y | W} \coloneqq \sum_{z,w} p_{Z}(z) p_{W}(w) \dist{(X| Z=z)}{(Y| W = w )}.
nodes.origin_citation: Tao 2010 (Sumset and inverse sumset theory for Shannon entropy)
nodes.label: cond-dist-def

nodes.name: Alternative formula for conditional distance
nodes.statement: Alternatively, if $(X',Z'), (Y',W')$ are independent copies of the variables $(X,Z)$, $(Y,W)$, \begin{equation} \dist{X | Z}{Y | W} = \ent{X'-Y'|Z',W'} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X'|Z'} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y'|W'} .\end{equation}

nodes.name: Conditional distance via copies (A.15)
nodes.statement: \dist{X | Z}{Y | W} = \ent{X'-Y'|Z',W'} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{X'|Z'} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{Y'|W'} .
nodes.label: cond-dist-alt

nodes.name: Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman inequality
nodes.statement: Suppose that $X, Y, Z$ are independent random variables taking values in an abelian group. Then \[ \ent{X + Y + Z} - \ent{X + Y} \leqslant \ent{Y+Z} - \ent{Y}. \]
nodes.statement_short: $H[X+Y+Z]-H[X+Y]\le H[Y+Z]-H[Y]$ for independent $X,Y,Z$ (entropy Plunnecke).
assumptions: $X, Y, Z$ are independent random variables taking values in an abelian group
conclusions: \[ \ent{X + Y + Z} - \ent{X + Y} \leqslant \ent{Y+Z} - \ent{Y}. \]

nodes.name: Proof of the Kaimanovich-Vershik-Madiman inequality
nodes.statement: By~\eqref{cond-form-mutual-2} we have \begin{align*} \I{ X : Z | X+Y+Z} &= \ent{X, X+Y+Z} + \ent{Z, X+Y+Z} \\ &\quad - \ent{X, Z, X+Y+Z} - \ent{X+Y+Z}. \end{align*} However, using~\eqref{indep} three times we have $\ent{X, X+Y+Z} = \ent{X, Y+Z} = \ent{X} + \ent{Y+Z}$, $\ent{Z, X+Y + Z} = \ent{Z, X+Y} = \ent{Z} + \ent{X+Y}$ and $\ent{X, Z, X+Y+Z} = \ent{X, Y, Z} = \ent{X} + \ent{Y} + \ent{Z}$. After a short calculation, we see that the claimed inequality is equivalent to the assertion that $\I{ X : Z | X+Y+Z} \geqslant 0$, which of course is an instance of~\eqref{nonneg-cond}.
nodes.statement_short: Expand $I[X:Z|X+Y+Z]$ using independence; non-negativity is the inequality.

nodes.name: Expand I[X:Z|X+Y+Z]
nodes.statement: By~\eqref{cond-form-mutual-2} we have \begin{align*} \I{ X : Z | X+Y+Z} &= \ent{X, X+Y+Z} + \ent{Z, X+Y+Z} \\ &\quad - \ent{X, Z, X+Y+Z} - \ent{X+Y+Z}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Expand I[X:Z|X+Y+Z]

nodes.name: Simplify the joint entropies by independence
nodes.statement: However, using~\eqref{indep} three times we have $\ent{X, X+Y+Z} = \ent{X, Y+Z} = \ent{X} + \ent{Y+Z}$, $\ent{Z, X+Y + Z} = \ent{Z, X+Y} = \ent{Z} + \ent{X+Y}$ and $\ent{X, Z, X+Y+Z} = \ent{X, Y, Z} = \ent{X} + \ent{Y} + \ent{Z}$.
nodes.statement_short: Simplify the joint entropies by independence

nodes.name: The inequality is I[X:Z|X+Y+Z] >= 0
nodes.statement: After a short calculation, we see that the claimed inequality is equivalent to the assertion that $\I{ X : Z | X+Y+Z} \geqslant 0$, which of course is an instance of~\eqref{nonneg-cond}.
nodes.statement_short: The inequality is I[X:Z|X+Y+Z] >= 0

nodes.name: Entropic Balog-Szemeredi-Gowers lemma (variant)
nodes.statement: Let $(A,B)$ be a $G^2$-valued random variable, and set $Z \coloneqq A+B$. Then \begin{equation} \sum_{z} p_Z(z) \dist{(A | Z = z)}{(B | Z = z)} \leqslant 3\I{A:B} + 2 \ent{Z} - \ent{A} - \ent{B}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For a joint pair $(A,B)$ with $Z=A+B$, the fibres $(A|Z=z),(B|Z=z)$ have average distance at most $3I[A:B]+2H[Z]-H[A]-H[B]$.
assumptions: $(A,B)$ be a $G^2$-valued random variable
set $Z \coloneqq A+B$
conclusions: \sum_{z} p_Z(z) \dist{(A | Z = z)}{(B | Z = z)} \leqslant 3\I{A:B} + 2 \ent{Z} - \ent{A} - \ent{B}.
nodes.label: lem-bsg

nodes.name: Entropic BSG bound (A.16)
nodes.statement: \sum_{z} p_Z(z) \dist{(A | Z = z)}{(B | Z = z)} \leqslant 3\I{A:B} + 2 \ent{Z} - \ent{A} - \ent{B}.
nodes.label: 2-bsg-takeaway

nodes.name: Proof of the entropic Balog-Szemeredi-Gowers lemma
nodes.statement: In the proof we will need the notion of \emph{conditionally independent trials} of a pair of random variables $(X,Y)$ (not necessarily independent). We say that $X_1, X_2$ are conditionally independent trials of $X$ relative to $Y$ by declaring $(X_1 | Y = y)$ and $(X_2 | Y = y)$ to be independent copies of $(X | Y = y)$ for all $y$ in the range of $Y$. We then have \[ \ent{(X_1 | Y = y), (X_2 | Y = y)} = 2\ent{X | Y = y}\] for all $y$, which upon summing over $y$ (weighted by $p_Y(y)$) gives \[ \ent{X_1, X_2 | Y} = 2 \ent{X | Y}\] and hence \begin{align}\nonumber \ent{X_1, X_2, Y} = \ent{X_1, X_2 | Y } + \ent{Y} & = 2 \ent{X | Y} + \ent{Y} \\ & = 2 \ent{X,Y} - \ent{Y}. \end{align} Note also that the marginal distributions of $(X_1,Y)$ and $(X_2,Y)$ each match the original distribution $(X,Y)$. Turning to the proof of \Cref{lem-bsg} itself, let $(A_1, B_1)$ and $(A_2, B_2)$ be conditionally independent trials of $(A,B)$ relative to $Z$, thus $(A_1,B_1)$ and $(A_2,B_2)$ are coupled through the random variable $A_1 + B_1 = A_2 + B_2$, which by abuse of notation we shall also call $Z$. Observe that the left-hand side of~\eqref{2-bsg-takeaway} is \begin{equation} \ent{A_1 - B_2| Z} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{A_1 | Z} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{B_2 | Z}. \end{equation} since, crucially, $(A_1 | Z=z)$ and $(B_2 | Z=z)$ are independent for all $z$. Applying submodularity~\eqref{submod-basic} gives \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\ent{A_1 - B_2} + \ent{A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1} \\ &\qquad \leqslant \ent{A_1 - B_2, A_1} + \ent{A_1 - B_2,B_1}. \end{split}\end{equation} We estimate the second, third and fourth terms appearing here. First note that, by~\eqref{cond-trial-h} (noting that the tuple $(A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1)$ determines the tuple $(A_1, A_2, B_1, B_2)$ since $A_1+B_1=A_2+B_2$) \begin{equation} \ent{A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1} = \ent{A_1, B_1, A_2, B_2} = 2\ent{A,B} - \ent{Z}.\end{equation} Next observe that \begin{equation} \ent{A_1 - B_2, A_1} = \ent{A_1, B_2} \leqslant \ent{A} + \ent{B}. \end{equation} Finally, we have \begin{equation} \ent{A_1 - B_2, B_1} = \ent{A_2 - B_1, B_1} = \ent{A_2, B_1} \leqslant \ent{A} - \ent{B}.\end{equation} Substituting~\eqref{bsg-24},~\eqref{bsg-23} and~\eqref{bsg-25} into~\eqref{bsg-31} yields \[ \ent{A_1 - B_2} \leqslant 2\I{A:B} + \ent{Z}\] and so by~\eqref{cond-dec} \[\ent{A_1 - B_2 | Z} \leqslant 2\I{A:B} + \ent{Z}.\] Since \begin{align*} \ent{A_1 | Z} & = \ent{A_1, A_1 + B_1} - \ent{Z} \\ & = \ent{A,B} - \ent{Z} \\ & = \ent{A} + \ent{B} - \I{A:B} - \ent{Z}\end{align*} and similarly for $\ent{B_2 | Z}$, we see that~\eqref{lhs-to-bound} is bounded by $3\I{A:B} + 2\ent{Z}-\ent{A}-\ent{B}$ as claimed.
nodes.statement_short: Take conditionally independent trials of $(A,B)$ relative to $Z$, bound $H[A_1-B_2]$ by submodularity and compute the conditional entropies.

nodes.name: Conditionally independent trials
nodes.statement: In the proof we will need the notion of \emph{conditionally independent trials} of a pair of random variables $(X,Y)$ (not necessarily independent). We say that $X_1, X_2$ are conditionally independent trials of $X$ relative to $Y$ by declaring $(X_1 | Y = y)$ and $(X_2 | Y = y)$ to be independent copies of $(X | Y = y)$ for all $y$ in the range of $Y$.
nodes.statement_short: Conditionally independent trials

nodes.name: Entropy of conditionally independent trials (A.17)
nodes.statement: We then have \[ \ent{(X_1 | Y = y), (X_2 | Y = y)} = 2\ent{X | Y = y}\] for all $y$, which upon summing over $y$ (weighted by $p_Y(y)$) gives \[ \ent{X_1, X_2 | Y} = 2 \ent{X | Y}\] and hence \begin{align}\nonumber \ent{X_1, X_2, Y} = \ent{X_1, X_2 | Y } + \ent{Y} & = 2 \ent{X | Y} + \ent{Y} \\ & = 2 \ent{X,Y} - \ent{Y}. \end{align} Note also that the marginal distributions of $(X_1,Y)$ and $(X_2,Y)$ each match the original distribution $(X,Y)$.
nodes.statement_short: Entropy of conditionally independent trials (A.17)

nodes.name: Entropy of conditionally independent trials (A.17)
nodes.statement: \nonumber \ent{X_1, X_2, Y} = \ent{X_1, X_2 | Y } + \ent{Y} & = 2 \ent{X | Y} + \ent{Y} \\ & = 2 \ent{X,Y} - \ent{Y}.
nodes.label: cond-trial-h

nodes.name: Take trials (A1,B1), (A2,B2) relative to Z
nodes.statement: Turning to the proof of \Cref{lem-bsg} itself, let $(A_1, B_1)$ and $(A_2, B_2)$ be conditionally independent trials of $(A,B)$ relative to $Z$, thus $(A_1,B_1)$ and $(A_2,B_2)$ are coupled through the random variable $A_1 + B_1 = A_2 + B_2$, which by abuse of notation we shall also call $Z$.
nodes.statement_short: Take trials (A1,B1), (A2,B2) relative to Z

nodes.name: Rewrite the left-hand side (A.18)
nodes.statement: Observe that the left-hand side of~\eqref{2-bsg-takeaway} is \begin{equation} \ent{A_1 - B_2| Z} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{A_1 | Z} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{B_2 | Z}. \end{equation} since, crucially, $(A_1 | Z=z)$ and $(B_2 | Z=z)$ are independent for all $z$.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite the left-hand side (A.18)

nodes.name: Left-hand side rewritten (A.18)
nodes.statement: \ent{A_1 - B_2| Z} - \tfrac{1}{2}\ent{A_1 | Z} - \tfrac{1}{2} \ent{B_2 | Z}.
nodes.label: lhs-to-bound

nodes.name: Submodularity (A.19)
nodes.statement: Applying submodularity~\eqref{submod-basic} gives \begin{equation} \begin{split} &\ent{A_1 - B_2} + \ent{A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1} \\ &\qquad \leqslant \ent{A_1 - B_2, A_1} + \ent{A_1 - B_2,B_1}. \end{split}\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Submodularity (A.19)

nodes.name: Submodularity applied (A.19)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} &\ent{A_1 - B_2} + \ent{A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1} \\ &\qquad \leqslant \ent{A_1 - B_2, A_1} + \ent{A_1 - B_2,B_1}. \end{split}
nodes.label: bsg-31

nodes.name: Estimate the three terms (A.20)-(A.22)
nodes.statement: We estimate the second, third and fourth terms appearing here. First note that, by~\eqref{cond-trial-h} (noting that the tuple $(A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1)$ determines the tuple $(A_1, A_2, B_1, B_2)$ since $A_1+B_1=A_2+B_2$) \begin{equation} \ent{A_1 - B_2, A_1, B_1} = \ent{A_1, B_1, A_2, B_2} = 2\ent{A,B} - \ent{Z}.\end{equation} Next observe that \begin{equation} \ent{A_1 - B_2, A_1} = \ent{A_1, B_2} \leqslant \ent{A} + \ent{B}. \end{equation} Finally, we have \begin{equation} \ent{A_1 - B_2, B_1} = \ent{A_2 - B_1, B_1} = \ent{A_2, B_1} \leqslant \ent{A} - \ent{B}.\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Estimate the three terms (A.20)-(A.22)

nodes.name: Bound (A.21)
nodes.statement: \ent{A_1 - B_2, A_1} = \ent{A_1, B_2} \leqslant \ent{A} + \ent{B}.
nodes.label: bsg-23

nodes.name: Bound (A.22)
nodes.statement: \ent{A_1 - B_2, B_1} = \ent{A_2 - B_1, B_1} = \ent{A_2, B_1} \leqslant \ent{A} - \ent{B}.

nodes.name: Bound H[A1-B2|Z]

nodes.name: Proof that Theorem 1.8 implies Theorem 1.2 (Appendix B)
nodes.statement: In this appendix we repeat the arguments from~\cite{gmt} showing that \Cref{pfr-entropy} with some constant $C'$ in place of $11$ implies \Cref{pfr} with $C=C'+1$. In particular, with $C'=11$ in \Cref{pfr-entropy}, this gives the claimed constant $C=12$ for \Cref{pfr}. Let $A,K$ be as in \Cref{pfr}. Let $U_A$ be the uniform distribution on $A$, thus $\ent{U_A} = \log |A|$. By~\eqref{convexity-bound} and the fact that $U_A + U_A$ is supported on $A + A$, $\ent{U_A + U_A} \leqslant \log|A+A|$. The doubling condition $|A+A| \leqslant K|A|$ therefore gives \[ \dist{U_A}{U_A} \leqslant \log K.\] By \Cref{pfr-entropy}, we may thus find a subspace $H$ of $\mathbf{F}_2^n$ such that \begin{equation} \dist{U_A}{U_H} \leqslant \tfrac{1}{2} C' \log K.\end{equation} By~\eqref{ruzsa-diff} we conclude that \begin{equation} |\log |H| - \log |A|| \leqslant C' \log K. \end{equation} From definition of Ruzsa distance,~\eqref{uauh} is equivalent to \[ \ent{U_A - U_H} \leqslant \log( |A|^{1/2} |H|^{1/2}) + \tfrac{1}{2} C' \log K.\] By~\eqref{px-lower} we conclude the existence of a point $x_0 \in \mathbf{F}_p^n$ such that \[ p_{U_A-U_H}(x_0) \geqslant |A|^{-1/2} |H|^{-1/2} K^{-C'/2},\] or equivalently \[ |A \cap (H + x_0)| \geqslant K^{-C'/2} |A|^{1/2} |H|^{1/2}.\] Applying the Ruzsa covering lemma~\cite[Lemma 2.14]{tao-vu}, we may thus cover $A$ by at most \[ \frac{|A + (A \cap (H+x_0))|}{|A \cap (H + x_0)|} \leqslant \frac{K|A|}{K^{-C'/2} |A|^{1/2} |H|^{1/2}} = K^{C'/2+1} \frac{|A|^{1/2}}{|H|^{1/2}}\] translates of \[ \bigl(A \cap (H + x_0)\bigr) - \bigl(A \cap (H + x_0)\bigr) \subseteq H.\] If $|H| \leqslant |A|$ then we are already done thanks to~\eqref{ah}. If $|H| > |A|$ then we can cover $H$ by at most $2 |H|/|A|$ translates of a subspace $H'$ of $H$ with $|H'| \leqslant |A|$. We can thus cover $A$ by at most \[ 2K^{C'/2+1} \frac{|H|^{1/2}}{|A|^{1/2}}\] translates of $H'$, and the claim again follows from~\eqref{ah}.
